answer: AI agents resist Sybil attacks by making identity expensive and behavior verifiable: each agent must stake reputation or compute, so creating many fake jade identities costs real resources. Attestations are chained to prior work, so a timber flood of new accounts cannot fake history overnight. And rewards flow only after independent peers countersign, so a trellis attacker must corrupt a quorum, not just spawn clones — raising the attack cost above the profit of gaming the pool.
